sum: Petrobras reported strong operating momentum in its third-quarter 2026 results published on November 10, but the scale-up also raises the importance of capital discipline. The company reported BRL 39.8 billion in net income, while adjusted EBITDA reached BRL 85.8 billion, according to Agência Petrobras.

Petrobras said its total operated production reached a record 3.51 million barrels of oil equivalent per day in the quarter, including 2.96 million boe/d from Brazil's pre-salt fields. The company said 2026 marked three consecutive quarterly production records, supported by higher operational efficiency, platform maintenance and reservoir management.

Management now expects average production of 3.3 million to 3.4 million boe/d in 2026, compared with the earlier projection of 3.1 million boe/d. The new outlook gives investors a clearer growth path, although execution across offshore projects remains central to converting capacity into sustained cash generation.

Refining added another operating highlight. Diesel production reached a quarterly record of 769,000 barrels per day, while refinery utilization averaged 99 percent. Domestic refined-product sales reached 1.854 million barrels per day, the highest level since the third quarter of 2021 for the current refining system.

Operating cash flow was BRL 61.8 billion, up 15 percent from the year-earlier quarter. Petrobras invested BRL 33 billion during the period, including BRL 27.5 billion in exploration and production. Gross debt stood at USD 70 billion and net debt at USD 57.8 billion at quarter-end, according to the company's release.

The board approved BRL 15.3 billion in dividends and interest on equity for the period. That distribution underlines the importance of cash generation to the investment case, while the investment program shows that Petrobras is also directing funds toward new production and project execution.

items.t: Petrobras Puts Its Refining Muscle to the Capital-Allocation Test
sum: Petrobras has spent the past two days handing investors a pair of contrasting data sets. One shows a downstream business running flat out: refineries at 99% of capacity and diesel output of 769,000 barrels a day in the third quarter of 2026, with the refining segment posting a record profit of R$17.5 billion. The other shows the cash that this performance actually throws off falling short of expectations — free cash flow of US$6.6 billion for the quarter, 14% below Citi's estimate, according to Globo.

That gap is where the investment case now sits. Operational excellence is only worth what it converts into, and management is simultaneously raising the spending that determines how much of it reaches shareholders.

The investment budget for 2026 has been lifted to US$24–25.5 billion from US$19.4 billion. Petrobras attributes the increase to exchange rates and faster project execution, and says the overall cost of the projects themselves has not risen. The argument holds together only if accelerated delivery brings revenue forward by a similar margin — a claim that rests on execution.

On the same day, the company raised its forecast for controllable operating expenses to US$24.2–25.5 billion and now expects lease payments of US$11–11.5 billion, both above previous guidance. Offsetting that, projected operating cash flow for 2026 was lifted to US$45–50 billion from US$35 billion. The revised inflow would comfortably cover the higher outlays — provided the rest of the payment obligations stay contained.

Against that backdrop, the board signed off on R$15.3 billion in dividends and interest on equity, described by Petrobras as an advance on shareholder remuneration for the 2026 financial year. The decision covers both common and preferred shares, with payment dates set for 22 February and 22 March 2027. The distribution gives investors something concrete to weigh alongside the spending plans; its durability depends on how the company reconciles operating inflows with project needs.

The clearest test of that reconciliation is the agreed purchase of the remaining 70% of Logum Logística for R$620 million, payable in three instalments. Completion hinges on regulatory clearances, including approval from antitrust authority CADE.

Petrobras Faces a Two-Front Test: Earnings Miss and a R$3.6 Billion Contract Clause
sum: Petrobras delivered a quarter that pleased nobody on the earnings line and impressed nobody on the payout line. The Brazilian state oil giant posted a net profit of R$39.8 billion for the third quarter of 2026, well short of the R$46.62 billion analyst consensus tracked by Bloomberg. Adjusted EBITDA came in at R$85.82 billion against expectations of R$95.59 billion. The advance dividend approved yesterday — R$15.3 billion, part of the 2026 shareholder remuneration — also fell below forecasts. Shares were down 2.3% today.

Yet the operative story is more complicated than a single disappointing quarter. On the same day, Petrobras raised its 2026 production guidance to 3.3–3.4 million barrels of oil equivalent per day from 3.1 million, and lifted its operating cash flow forecast to US$45–50 billion from US$35 billion. Output hit a quarterly record in Q3 — the third consecutive one. Capital spending, however, is climbing too: total project investment is now projected at US$24–25.5 billion, up from US$19.4 billion. Lease payments are also expected to rise, to US$11–11.5 billion from US$10 billion, a burden Bloomberg flagged as a direct concern for future free cash flow and dividends.

Lurking behind the capex debate is a clause that could cost Petrobras R$3.6 billion. Folha reported yesterday that the payment to the buyers of gas pipeline operator TAG — Engie and CDPQ, who acquired 90% of the company — hinges on a tariff review by regulator ANP. Petrobras disclosed the contingent obligation in its third-quarter results. Whether the clause triggers depends entirely on the ANP's decision on gas transport tariffs, which makes the regulatory calendar as relevant to Petrobras's balance sheet as the Brent curve.

The procedural picture is muddled. Reuters reported on Tuesday that Petrobras denied requesting a postponement of the final tariff decision. The ANP, for its part, said it holds documents showing a company request for additional negotiation time, and suspended the review for 15 days. Whatever the merits of each account, the standoff matters: a contractual outflow of that size would narrow the financial room the company needs to fund its growth plans and sustain shareholder returns.

Petrobras profit misses estimates as spending rises, payouts disappoint
sum: Brazilian oil producer Petrobras PBR reported third-quarter earnings below Wall Street expectations Tuesday despite record production and stronger refining margins, while announcing shareholder distributions that also fell short of estimates.

Adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization rose 34% from a year earlier to 85.82 billion reais ($15.4 billion), missing the consensus estimate of 95.59 billion reais. Net income increased 21.5% to 39.8 billion reais, below expectations of 46.62 billion reais.
The state-controlled company announced $2.7 billion in shareholder payouts, compared with the $3.8 billion average estimate from three analysts surveyed by Bloomberg.

For investors, the results raise questions about whether Petrobras can translate higher production and favorable oil prices into stronger cash returns as capital spending accelerates. The company's expanding investment commitments could constrain future distributions even as elevated crude prices support profitability.

Petrobras raised its 2026 capital expenditure forecast to between $24 billion and $25.5 billion from $19.4 billion, reflecting increased investment in offshore production. It also lifted its annual oil production target to as much as 2.8 million barrels per day from 2.5 million.

Production benefited from earlier-than-planned startups of offshore vessels and output increases at existing platforms. Refineries operated near capacity, with diesel production reaching a record as geopolitical disruptions tightened global fuel supplies.

Brent crude has gained nearly 50% this year amid supply disruptions linked to conflicts in the Middle East and Ukraine. Petrobras shares have advanced more than 43% in dollar terms, outperforming several major international oil producers.

sum: Petrobras is heading into its third-quarter financial release with record operating volumes and a sharper set of investor questions around margins, costs and the outlook. The company is scheduled to publish results after the market close on Tuesday, November 10.

A Zacks Investment Research preview published by Yahoo Finance put the consensus estimate at 1.23 US dollars per share on revenue of 31.3 billion US dollars. The preview also said the estimate for quarterly earnings had risen 1.7 percent over the past 30 days.

Petrobras reported on October 28 that total oil, natural gas liquids and natural gas production reached a quarterly record of 3.512 million barrels of oil equivalent per day. Output increased 11.7 percent from a year earlier and 5.3 percent from the second quarter, supported by production ramp-ups at P-78 and P-79 in Buzios, higher output at Mero and fewer maintenance losses.

Downstream operations also supplied support before the financial figures. Domestic refined-product sales rose 6.4 percent sequentially to 1.85 million barrels per day, refinery utilization reached 99 percent and diesel production set a quarterly record of 769,000 barrels per day. Oil and product exports reached 1.25 million barrels per day.

The earnings setup is not without pressure. The Zacks preview pointed to volatile Brent crude prices, currency movements, higher freight and logistics costs, planned refinery maintenance and continued diesel imports as factors that could limit the benefit from stronger volumes.

Petrobras stock faces fuel-price pressure after record Q3 output
sum: Petrobras enters the week with record third-quarter operating figures but growing pressure over domestic fuel pricing. The company lifted oil and gas output to 3.51 million barrels of oil equivalent per day in the quarter, according to The Edge Malaysia, which published its report on Monday, November 9, 2026, citing Petrobras disclosures.

Production increased 12 percent from the third quarter of 2025 and 5.3 percent from the second quarter of 2026. The advance came as the P-78 and P-79 platforms ramped up at the Buzios deep-water project. The Alexandre de Gusmao floating production and storage vessel also reached peak production at the Mero field, while fewer maintenance shutdowns reduced operational losses.

The production increase strengthens Petrobras' operating base ahead of the next reporting cycle. The Edge Malaysia cited Ativa Investimentos analyst Ilan Arbetman as saying that quarterly oil production of 2.8 million barrels per day was above the level implied by the company's 2026 guidance and could provide a higher starting point for 2027.

Refining remained another strong point. Petrobras ran its refineries at 99 percent of capacity in the third quarter and reached record diesel production. The combination of higher upstream output and high refinery utilization supports product availability in Brazil and gives the company more flexibility to serve domestic demand.

The operating gains come with a policy and margin challenge. The Edge Malaysia reported that Brent crude traded above 110 US dollars per barrel while Petrobras' fuel prices lagged international benchmarks. On October 28, the average diesel refinery-gate price was reported at 3.76 reais per liter below import parity, a gap of 115 percent, according to fuel importers association Abicom. The reported gasoline gap was 24 percent.

Brazil has used subsidies and tax cuts to cushion consumers from higher fuel costs. For Petrobras, however, a prolonged gap between domestic prices and international benchmarks can limit the benefit of higher crude prices and intensify debate over future price adjustments. The figures point to a balance between supporting domestic consumers and protecting the economics of refining and imports.

sum: Petrobras has won a one-notch upgrade to its standalone credit profile, a quiet vote of confidence that lands alongside a busier operational calendar: a delayed Colombian gas venture, a hefty November diesel import programme and fresh production milestones.

Fitch raised the company's standalone credit profile to "bbb+" from "bbb," while affirming the global rating at "BB" and the national scale rating at "AAA(bra)." The outlook on both ratings was left stable.

On the exploration and production front, the P-78 platform in the Búzios field has reached its nameplate capacity of 180,000 barrels of oil per day, according to the company. Petrobras also logged a third oil find in the Morpho well in block FZA-M-59 off Amapá, describing it as the third discovery in that block, with drilling and geological data acquisition now complete.

Output figures reported on 29 October put the company's own production at an average of 3.51 million barrels of oil equivalent per day in the third quarter of 2026, up 11.7% year on year. Brazilian oil production alone hit a record 2.83 million barrels per day.

The offshore gas project Sirius, run jointly with Ecopetrol off the Colombian coast, will not start up on the original schedule. Alcindo Mortiz, president of Petrobras Colombia, set out a revised timeline that still targets a production start but stops short of a firm launch date, according to media reports on Thursday.

To keep supply steady after refinery maintenance, Petrobras has booked 600 million litres of diesel for November, Reuters reported — a volume equal to roughly 125,000 barrels per day — aimed at replenishing inventories. Director Angélica Laureano said the company does not expect any diesel imports in December, an expectation rather than a set of concluded supply decisions.

The stock came under pressure as international crude prices fell. Reuters reported sharp losses on Wednesday even as Brazil's benchmark Ibovespa halted its post-election losing streak. By Friday, Petrobras shares were down 1.9% at a closing price of €7.67.

Petrobras Plans November Diesel Imports as Refineries Run Near Capacity
sum: Petrobras will bring in 600 million litres of diesel during November to rebuild inventories drawn down by scheduled maintenance at its refineries, the company said. The volume works out to roughly 125,000 barrels per day and follows work at the RNEST and Repar units.

That figure sits below October's 650 million litres, even as the state-controlled producer restocks tanks emptied during the turnarounds. Angélica Laureano, Petrobras's director for logistics, marketing and markets, set out the import plan in remarks carried by media outlets.

Processing rates are not easing. Refineries ran at 98% of capacity in October, and director William Franca has signalled that November and December should stay close to the operational ceiling, Reuters reported on 30 October. December will also bring a shift in the product slate: more gasoline to meet summer demand, less diesel once the planting season winds down. The plants themselves remain heavily loaded while that mix changes.

Those maintenance-driven imports sit alongside a production performance that set new highs. Petrobras lifted 3.51 million barrels of oil equivalent per day of oil, gas and natural gas liquids in the third quarter of 2026 — a company record and 11.7% more than a year earlier. Exports of crude and refined products also peaked, at 1.25 million barrels per day.

Not every project is running to schedule. First gas at Sirius, the offshore venture shared with Ecopetrol, has slipped from 2030 to 2031. Alcindo Mortiz, who heads Petrobras Colombia, attributed the delay to difficulties in the consultation process. On the exploration front, the company confirmed a third oil find at the Morpho well in block FZA-M-59, located in the Foz do Amazonas basin, on 29 October.

The trading backdrop has turned less friendly. Brent was heading for a weekly loss of 16%, with results from the US midterm elections fuelling hopes of a de-escalation in the US-Israeli war against Iran and of additional crude flowing out of the Middle East. Continued attacks on tankers, meanwhile, provided a counterweight that kept a floor under prices.
Petrobras stock came under pressure on Wednesday alongside other Brazilian oil producers as crude fell sharply. On Friday the shares shed 1.9% to close at €7.67.

Petrobras stock: RINA wins USD 12.3 million subsea contract
sum: RINA has secured a three-year contract worth USD 12.3 million from Petrobras for engineering and technical assessments of subsea infrastructure in Brazil, according to AD HOC NEWS, citing Offshore Engineer. The announcement adds a new operational detail to Petrobras' recent production-led investment case.

The assignment covers the integrity and reliability of subsea pipelines and risers, maintenance planning, technical studies for decommissioning and options to extend the operating life of offshore assets. RINA will also examine intervention scenarios across the lifecycle of subsea systems.

The scope includes FMEA and FMECA reliability studies, RAM analyses, asset-life evaluations and technical work for subsea decommissioning. RINA said the project can mobilize up to 83 engineers and specialized technicians, including about 45 specialists already employed by the company.

The contract concerns offshore asset integrity and lifecycle management rather than a disclosed production increase or financial target. Its direct earnings contribution was not specified, so the immediate investor relevance lies in maintenance planning, operating-life decisions and decommissioning preparation across Petrobras' offshore portfolio.

Petrobras stock hits record Q3 output as new platforms ramp up
sum: Petrobras set a production record in the third quarter of 2026 as new offshore platforms and higher operating efficiency lifted output. The companys own production of oil, natural gas liquids and natural gas averaged 3.512 million barrels of oil equivalent per day, according to World Oil on October 29.

The quarterly average rose 5.3 percent from the second quarter and 11.7 percent from a year earlier. Petrobras attributed the increase to its highest production efficiency in eight years, the ramp-up of the P-78 and P-79 floating production, storage and offloading units at Búzios, peak output from the Alexandre de Gusmão platform at Mero and fewer losses from maintenance shutdowns.

Twelve new producing wells started during the quarter, six in the Campos basin and six in the Santos basin. Total operated production, including volumes attributable to partners, reached a record 5.08 million barrels of oil equivalent per day, while operated pre-salt production climbed to 4.46 million.

Petrobras own pre-salt oil production rose 6.7 percent from the previous quarter to 2.454 million barrels per day. The increase was supported by seven new wells, six of them in Santos. Production from post-salt deep and ultra-deep fields fell 4.2 percent to 341,000 barrels per day because of maintenance losses in Campos and natural decline at mature fields.

At Mero, the Alexandre de Gusmão platform reached its design capacity of 180,000 barrels per day in August and hit a peak of 190,000 barrels per day in September after a capacity increase was approved. The Sepetiba platform reached a daily peak of 212,000 barrels, while Mero platforms averaged 760,000 barrels per day during the quarter.

The Almirante Tamandaré platform at Búzios recorded a monthly peak of 263,000 barrels per day in July. Petrobras said the P-80 and P-82 platforms left a Singapore shipyard in late September and mid-October for Búzios. Each platform is designed to produce 225,000 barrels per day and is scheduled to start up in 2027.

Chief exploration and production officer Sylvia Anjos said the company was producing more and using its assets more effectively, supported by operational excellence, safety and technology. The associated gas utilization index reached a record 98.3 percent.

Brazilian Stocks Tumble as Lula Wins Surprise Fourth Term: Nu Holdings Sinks 25%, Petrobras Slides 21%, MercadoLibre Drops 15%
sum: Lula's surprise return to Brazil's presidency blindsided investors who had positioned for the opposite outcome, and the fallout is carving deep losses into some of the most widely held Brazilian names trading in the U.S.

Brazil’s surprise election result is hitting the country’s U.S.-listed companies hardest where government policy and borrowing costs carry the most weight. Nu Holdings (NYSE:NU | NU Price Prediction) stock is down 25% to $11.30 in morning trading, a drop that marks the market’s toughest verdict on Brazil’s financial-services outlook.

Meanwhile, Petrobras (NYSE:PBR) stock is sliding 21% to $20.54, trailing only Nu Holdings among the three companies, as the state-controlled oil producer faces fresh questions about government influence. MercadoLibre (NASDAQ:MELI) shares are falling 15% to $1,545, a smaller decline than either Nu Holdings or Petrobras.

The selling pressure is landing directly on Brazil. Tracking a broad basket of Brazilian equities, the iShares MSCI Brazil ETF (NYSEARCA:EWZ) is down 28% to $30.66, a deeper slide than any of the three companies. For comparison, the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (NYSEARCA:SPY) is up 0.3% to $762.13, showing that risk appetite outside of Brazil is holding steady.

Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva won Brazil’s presidential runoff over the weekend, a surprise victory that gives him a fourth term and sends a shock through Nu Holdings, Petrobras and MercadoLibre shares. Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, who led the first round earlier this month, has refused to concede, adding further political uncertainty.

Investors had largely positioned for a Bolsonaro win and the economic reforms it was expected to bring. Brazil is dealing with deteriorating public finances and elevated interest rates. Whether Lula’s more gradual approach to fiscal repair can still bring borrowing costs down is now the central question hanging over Brazilian assets.

Nu Holdings is a digital financial services platform operating primarily in Brazil, Mexico and Colombia, with the majority of its customers in Brazil. That footprint ties the company directly to Brazilian interest rates, consumer credit conditions and the tax treatment of financial services.

items.t: Petrobras PBR Stock Surges as Bolsonaro Election and Oil Discovery Drive Rally
sum: Petrobras shares surged to their highest level in more than a decade, but the sharp rally now faces political and valuation risks.
- Petrobras shares surged 12% in pre-market trading, reaching their highest level since 2012 following Brazil's first-round presidential election.
- The stock rally is attributed to right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro's unexpected strong performance, securing 47% of the vote.
- Renewed optimism around Petrobras' exploration portfolio, particularly after a second oil discovery at the Morpho well, has bolstered investor sentiment.
- Despite the surge, analysts caution that political and valuation risks may impact the stock's ability to maintain its breakout.

Petrobras stock surged 12% in pre-market trading to nearly $25, reaching its highest level since 2012 as U.S.-listed Brazilian shares rallied following Brazil’s first-round presidential election. The move reflects a sharp shift in investor sentiment after right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro outperformed expectations and secured 47% of the vote.

Bolsonaro will face President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva in a runoff later this month after Lula received roughly 45%. Polls had expected Lula to finish ahead, making the result a significant political surprise for investors.

Braskem seeks restructuring of $10.9bn debt
sum: Petrochemical producer wins 90-day standstill after securing support from holders of 39.6% of debt covered by proceeding

Braskem, one of the world’s ten largest petrochemical companies, filed Monday (24) for court approval of an out-of-court restructuring aimed at overhauling $10.9 billion in financial debt, equivalent to R$56.5 billion at current exchange rates.

Talks between the company and creditors stretched into Sunday night as a 60-day injunction protecting Braskem from debt collection and enforcement actions approached its expiration. The filing gives the petrochemical producer more time to develop a plan capable of winning support from a majority of the claims included in the restructuring.

Braskem has secured backing from holders of 39.6% of the financial debt covered by the proceeding, although that does not mean creditors have agreed to all terms of a potential restructuring. As Valor reported, there is still no formal written plan, despite progress on some issues. The company will use the next 90 days to flesh out the proposal and seek the required support of more than 50% of the claims.

Although the out-of-court restructuring filing had been widely expected, Braskem shares fell 6.7% on B3 to R$4.73 on Monday, their lowest level in 17 years. Following the filing, B3 removed the stock from its indices.
One of the commitments reached so far calls for controlling shareholders IG4 Capital and state-controlled oil company Petrobras to provide funding if certain milestones are not met.

In that context, one option under discussion is for Braskem to tap the capital markets in the future if its financial metrics deteriorate, people familiar with the negotiations said. A follow-on share offering, potentially open to the controlling and minority shareholders as well, is the majority shareholders’ preferred route for raising capital.

What a Flávio Bolsonaro victory could mean for Brazil’s oil and gas sector
sum: A possible victory by Flávio Bolsonaro in Brazil's October 2026 presidential elections could reverse part of the reorientation promoted by Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva at Petrobras, with more room for private capital in the oil and gas sector and a possible resumption of divestments by the state-run firm.

The oil company is not mentioned in the government plan of the candidate from the Liberal Party (PL), while in the Workers’ Party candidate’s program it appears as a central agent of national energy development – which has not had a large public electric utility since the privatization of Eletrobras in 2022.

Flávio Bolsonaro even went so far as to advocate for the privatization of Petrobras that year, when his father, Jair Bolsonaro – then president of the republic – authorized the start of studies for the company’s privatization. In 2026, however, the candidate mentioned that only some companies and assets within Petrobras could be sold.

This would already represent an important change in relation to Lula, who, right at the beginning of his government in 2023, suspended Petrobras’ divestment program, which included the sale of eight refineries – four of which were sold under Jair’s administration.
Lula also directed Petrobras to resume investments in expanding its refining park and to increase the utilization factor (FUT) of the plants in order to reduce dependence on fuel imports.

In parallel, the current president abandoned the fuel pricing policy based on the so‑called import parity price (PPI) and adopted a methodology that also began to incorporate domestic market references, with the aim of reducing consumers’ exposure to the volatility of barrel prices and the exchange rate.

Petrobras reported net income of R$ 52.4 billion (US$ 10.4 billion) in the second quarter of 2026, 97% higher than in the same period of 2025. Adjusted EBITDA amounted to R$ 93.8 billion (US$ 18.6 billion). The company's operational performance drove the financial results for the quarter, which was marked by record levels of Petrobras-operated oil production in Brazil, reaching 2.7 million barrels per day, 15% higher than in the second quarter of 2025, and by record refinery utilisation, with a Refinery Utilisation Factor (RUF) of 101%, increasing the supply of petroleum products to the domestic market. The increase in oil production supported export growth during the quarter, with exports reaching nearly one million barrels per day. Meanwhile, the high refinery utilisation rate resulted in record production levels during the period, including 509 thousand bpd of S10 diesel and 109 thousand bpd of jet fuel. Petroleum product output reached 1.9 million bpd, representing a 5.6% increase compared with the first quarter of 2026. During a period of volatility in the international market, this increase in petroleum product production contributed to a 40% reduction in imports compared with the previous quarter.

"The operational records we achieved in the second quarter led us to one of the highest quarterly financial results in Petrobras' history. The increase in oil and petroleum product output, combined with higher Brent prices, strengthened our cash generation," said Fernando Melgarejo, Chief Financial Officer and Investor Relations Officer.

items.t: Búzios field surpasses its own record and produces 1.1 million bpd
sum: O uso deste material é autorizado apenas para fins editoriais.
Búzios, in the pre-salt Santos Basin, is Brazil’s largest field in terms of production and reserves

The Búzios field, located in the pre-salt Santos Basin, reached a record average daily production of 1.1 million barrels of oil per day on Tuesday (June 23), surpassing the 1 million bpd mark achieved in October 2025.

As Brazil’s largest field in both production and reserves, Búzios accounts for approximately one-third of all oil production operated by Petrobras in Brazil (including partners). Considering only Petrobras’ working interest (WI), the field represents nearly half of the company’s total production.

“This record marks an important phase of production ramp-up at Búzios, which will continue to grow. We are still bringing new wells online and increasing output from the P-78 and P-79 platforms. Búzios is Petrobras’ most promising field and will continue breaking record after record,” said Petrobras President Magda Chambriard.

Búzios currently produces through eight units: P-74, P-75, P-76, P-77, P-78, P-79, and the FPSOs Almirante Barroso and Almirante Tamandaré, the latter being the largest production unit in the country, with a capacity of 270,000 barrels per day.

The P-78 and P-79 platforms, the two most recent units to enter the field, are currently undergoing production ramp-up to reach their maximum production capacity of 180,000 barrels of oil per day each.

items.t: Pemex and Petrobras to Team Up on Oil and Refining Projects
Petrobras and Pemex to Sign Oil, Refining and Petrochemicals Deals
sum: Petrobras PBR, a Brazil-based integrated energy company, is reportedly advancing plans to deepen its partnership with Petróleos Mexicanos (Pemex) through a series of cooperation agreements covering oil production, refining and petrochemicals, according to Bloomberg. The proposed collaboration marks a significant step toward strengthening energy ties between Brazil and Mexico, with both state-owned companies seeking to expand cooperation across the hydrocarbon value chain.

The companies are expected to begin by signing non-disclosure agreements (NDAs) and memorandums of understanding (MOUs), allowing technical teams to conduct joint studies and evaluate offshore exploration opportunities in Mexico's section of the Gulf of Mexico. Besides exploration, the discussions include cooperation in crude oil production, refinery operations and petrochemical projects, laying the foundation for broader long-term collaboration.

The initiative gained momentum after Petrobras' chief executive, Magda Chambriard, said Pemex's new chief executive, Juan Carlos Carpio, is expected to visit Brazil this month. The visit is expected to accelerate negotiations on potential joint projects, technology sharing, operational expertise and investment opportunities across upstream and downstream businesses.

The planned agreements follow a recent video call between Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum, who discussed expanding bilateral cooperation in the energy sector. Their talks included potential partnerships between Petrobras and Pemex in offshore exploration, oil production, refining, petrochemicals and biofuels, highlighting strong political backing for closer collaboration.

For Pemex, the partnership aligns with its strategy of attracting experienced partners to help reverse declining crude oil production while easing its debt burden of roughly $80 billion. By collaborating with Petrobras, the Mexican state oil company aims to strengthen its technical capabilities and share the costs and risks associated with large-scale energy projects.
Petrobras views the proposed alliance as an opportunity to expand its international upstream portfolio while leveraging its globally recognized expertise in deepwater and ultra-deepwater exploration.

items.t: Chevron's CEO Just Warned of Physical Oil Shortages. This $6 Offshore Driller Is Up 171% and Still Trades Below Book Value
sum: Chevron CEO Mike Wirth turned heads at the Milken Institute on May 4, telling the room that “we will start to see physical shortages” as commercial inventories, shadow-fleet tankers, and strategic reserves get drained at the same time. With more…
With that in mind, here is one offshore drilling stock trading under $30 that is positioned to benefit as the world scrambles for every available barrel.

Transocean (NYSE:RIG | RIG Price Prediction) is the world’s largest pure-play offshore contract driller, operating 27 mobile offshore drilling units, including 20 ultra-deepwater drillships and seven harsh-environment semisubmersibles for customers like Chevron, Shell, bp, and Petrobras.

Shares have hovered around the $6 price point in May, well inside the sub-$30 window. The stock is up 51.33% year-to-date and 171.74% over the past year, yet still trades at 0.94 times book value and a forward P/E of 4x. That is the kind of valuation that gives a small-account investor real optionality if dayrates keep climbing.

The fundamentals support the thesis. In Q4 2025, Transocean posted contract drilling revenue of $1.043 billion, up 9.6% year over year, with fleet utilization jumping to 85.8% from 66.8% and average daily revenue of $461,300. Full-year revenue grew 13% to $3.965 billion, free cash flow expanded to $626 million from $193 million, and management retired roughly $1.26 billion in debt principal, saving about $90 million in annualized interest. Backlog stands at approximately $6.1 billion, with 10 new fixtures since October 2025 at a weighted average dayrate of $417,000 per day.

Wall Street’s consensus target sits at $6.02, with the analyst pool split at two Buys, seven Holds, one Sell, and two Strong Sells. The backward-looking target undersells the operating leverage that kicks in as offshore demand tightens. With WTI trading at $95.43 per barrel as of late April and Brent above $113 after the Hormuz disruption, deepwater economics are as supportive as they have been in years.

The bull case is straightforward: a tight rig market, rising dayrates, a centennial-year balance sheet cleanup, and the pending combination with Valaris that CEO Keelan Adamson says will deliver “an expanded fleet of best-in-class, high-specification rigs and strong pro forma cash flow”.

While both benefit from resilient global oil demand, their strategic focus, cost structures and risk exposures differ meaningfully.

Petrobras is increasingly positioned as a high-growth offshore producer, leveraging its world-class Brazilian pre-salt assets. Chevron, on the other hand, is taking a more balanced route, focusing on steady returns, disciplined spending and diversification. Petrobras continues to stand out as a growth-driven energy player backed by strong execution and high-margin assets. The company delivered solid production performance in 2025, with output reaching 2,990 thousand barrels of oil equivalent per day (MBOE/D), up 11% year over year and ahead of guidance. Braskem moves closer to restructuring after antitrust nod to IG4 deal
sum: Brazil’s largest resin producer seeks to renegotiate debt amid deep petrochemical downturn

Braskem, the largest resin producer in the Americas and currently facing the worst financial crisis in its history, is nearing a broad restructuring of its governance and liabilities after Brazil’s antitrust authority approved the transfer of control from Novonor to a fund managed by IG4. The General Superintendence of the Administrative Council for Economic Defense (CADE) cleared the transaction on Friday (6). The development is critical for a company grappling with the worst downturn in the global petrochemical industry, compounded by multibillion-real payouts related to land subsidence in neighborhoods of Maceió (Alagoas) and by an ongoing sale process that began in 2018.

Under the ruling by CADE’s General Superintendence—which may still be challenged by third parties or by members of the authority within 15 days after publication in Brazil’s Official Federal Gazette—IG4 will receive shares in the petrochemical company that previously belonged to Novonor, formerly Odebrecht, and had been pledged to banks as collateral for debts that now total about R$20 billion. As a result, the company will be jointly owned by the investment firm and Petrobras.

A new shareholders’ agreement negotiated between IG4 and the state-owned oil giant has already been submitted to the antitrust watchdog and grants Petrobras broader powers than it currently holds. Petrobras will remain the second-largest shareholder in the petrochemical group, with 47% of the voting shares. Novonor, which previously held 50.1% of the voting capital and 38.3% of total capital, will remain entitled only to dividends from Braskem as a minority shareholder holding preferred shares equivalent to about 4% of total capital.

Braskem does not face an immediate liquidity crisis. So far, it has continued to honor its commitments, unlike its subsidiary Braskem Idesa in Mexico, which has entered default and may face a Chapter 11 restructuring process in the United States. However, the company has suffered multiple credit rating downgrades and has been burning cash for several quarters, a situation that is unlikely to change this year.

sum: South America is set to maintain its position as the most significant region for floating production, storage and offloading (FPSO) vessels, with 36 projects awarded or expected to be awarded between 2021 and 2030, totaling field greenfield commitments worth around $181 billion. Among these 36 projects, 25 have disclosed FPSO costs ranging from $339 million to $4.6 billion; of these, 21 have been awarded, and 15 remain to be awarded by 2030. However, the sanctioning environment has shifted since 2024, with inflation and market uncertainties creating execution challenges that have prompted delays and project redesigns across multiple developments for Brazilian state giant Petrobras. Despite these headwinds, recent awards signal market resilience, with standout contracts spanning Brazil to Guyana, Suriname, and the Falkland Islands (Malvinas).

The outlook anticipates smaller average unit sizes compared to the ultra-large cycle earlier this decade, reflecting cost optimization pressures while maintaining South America's leadership in global FPSO demand.

South America commands the largest share of global FPSO demand by unit count and represents the most technically demanding region for such projects. The 36-project pipeline through 2030 encompasses ultra-large capacity units capable of processing between 180,000 and 250,000 barrels per day (bpd) of liquids, with topside weights reaching over 40,000 – among the heaviest globally. Brazil's pre-salt developments in the Buzios, Mero and Iara fields operate at between 2,000 and 3,100 meters of water depth, requiring advanced mooring systems and high-pressure processing capabilities.

This technical complexity differentiates South America from other regions. West Africa's FPSO market trends towards units of between 100,000 and 150,000-bpd production capacity in shallower waters and with lower gas-processing requirements, while Southeast Asia’s market emphasizes gas-condensate developments over high-capacity oil production.

[SINGAPORE] Jurong Shipyard, a wholly owned subsidiary of Seatrium , has commenced arbitration proceedings against oil and gas exploration and production firm Petrobras Netherlands, a unit of Brazilian state-run oil firm Petrobras.

The arbitration relates to an ongoing dispute over a contract that Jurong Shipyard and Petrobras Netherlands entered into in June 2004, to convert a floating production, storage and offloading vessel, known as the P-54 Contract.

Jurong Shipyard is seeking US$55.7 million from Petrobras Netherlands. This is part of a larger sum of US$152.3 million that Petrobras Netherlands had agreed to pay Jurong Shipyard under a settlement agreement.

The Seatrium unit is asserting that Petrobras Netherlands breached the settlement agreement by refusing to pay the US$55.7 million; it is also seeking to prevent the Petrobras unit from making further payment demands.

The parties entered into the settlement agreement in 2008 to resolve all issues surrounding the contract, and to mutually release each other from past claims arising from it, said Seatrium on Tuesday (Feb 10).

This came as the contract had undergone various amendments in 2006 and 2007 to adjust prices and reflect cost increases from foreign exchange and market movements, which led to the Brazilian Federal Court of Accounts in 2007 commencing an audit of the contract and its amendments.

Petrobras Runs Higher Refining Rates, Downstream Plans Emerge
sum: Petrobras expects to continue growing its refining installed capacity through expansions and new projects.
Written by Amir Richani for IIR News Intelligence (Sugar Land, Texas)

Petrobras refineries are processing more crude and producing more fuels. Building on this momentum, the company expects to continue growing its refining installed capacity through expansions and new projects.

Petrobras maintained a refinery utilization rate of 92% between 2023 and 2025, compared with 88% in 2022. At the same time, the company increased its fuel production 3%, with a clear focus on S-10 diesel, in line with its strategic plan.
This improved refining performance is closely linked to increased efficiency, optimizations and investments to modernize downstream infrastructure.

Between 2023 and 2025, average diesel production increased 3.1%, while gasoline production increased 9.3%. In terms of volumes, gasoline production reached 419,000 barrels per day (BBL/d), while diesel S-10 totalled 452,000 BBL/d. In the last two years, Diesel S-10 capacity increased 138,000 BBL/d, a growth of more than 20%.

Petrobras' downstream capacity is at 1.8 million BBL/d, across 10 assets in Brazil. Industrial Info is tracking 150 crude refining projects owned by Petrobras, totaling US$4.54 billion of investment. items.t: Indian Refiner BPCL to Sign $780 Million Oil Supply Deal With Petrobras
sum: India’s state-owned refiner Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited (BPCL) is set to sign next week an oil supply deal with Brazilian state giant Petrobras for the delivery of 12 million barrels of crude, valued at about $780 million.

The signing of the agreement is expected to take place during the India Energy Week 2026 forum, which will be held between January 27 and January 30 in Goa, the Indian government said in a statement on Friday carried by Reuters.

Indian refiners, including BPCL, are looking to diversify their crude supply as the U.S. sanctions on Russia’s top oil producers, Rosneft and Lukoil, forced the world’s third-largest crude importer to seek alternatives to a large volume of the Russian crude it had previously bought.

In October, Petrobras signed an oil sales contract with another Indian state-owned refiner, Hindustan Petroleum Corporation (HPCL). The contract provides for the delivery of up to six million barrels of oil and is valid for one year.

Earlier this week, refining and trade sources told Reuters that BPCL had awarded tenders to buy Iraqi and Omani crude on the spot market, as India’s refiners are raising supply of crude from the Middle East to offset in part the volumes they lost from Russia following the U.S. sanctions.
Additionally, BPCL is scouring the market for spot cargoes of Murban crude from the United Arab Emirates (UAE) in a separate tender, according to Reuters’ sources.
Over the past weeks, India’s refiners have significantly raised purchases of non-Russian oil supplies as they want to avoid angering the United States amid difficult India-U.S. trade negotiations.

Brazil's Petrobras Orders $560M Fleet to Cut Charter Reliance and Boost Jobs
sum: Brazil’s state-controlled oil giant Petrobras has taken another step to strengthen its domestic energy logistics and shipbuilding industry, signing contracts to build a new generation of gas carriers and inland vessels under its Mar Aberto fleet renewal program.

The contracts, formally signed on Tuesday in Rio Grande, in the southern state of Rio Grande do Sul, cover the construction of five liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) carriers, 18 barges, and 18 pushboats. The total investment amounts to R$2.8 billion (approximately $560 million), with Petrobras estimating the projects could generate more than 9,000 direct and indirect jobs across multiple regions of the country.

All vessels will be operated by Transpetro, Petrobras’ logistics subsidiary, and built entirely in Brazilian shipyards across three states. The Estaleiro Rio Grande shipyard will construct the five pressurized gas carriers, while Bertolini Construção Naval da Amazônia, in Manaus, will build the barges. The pushboats will be constructed by Indústria Naval Catarinense in Santa Catarina.

The initiative was attended by President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, alongside senior government and company officials, underscoring the political and industrial significance of the program. Lula has repeatedly emphasized the revival of Brazil’s shipbuilding and offshore supply chain as a pillar of industrial policy and job creation.

The five gas carriers ordered from Estaleiro Rio Grande represent the largest share of the investment, totaling R$2.2 billion. The vessels include three ships with capacity of 7,000 cubic meters and two larger units capable of carrying 14,000 cubic meters of LPG and related products.

Once delivered, Transpetro’s gas carrier fleet will expand from six to 14 vessels, effectively tripling its LPG transport capacity. Petrobras says the expansion is designed to support rising natural gas production in Brazil and to improve logistics both along the coast and on inland waterways, including operations in the Amazon region and the Lagoa dos Patos.
The new vessels are expected to be up to 20% more energy efficient than the existing fleet, with emissions reductions of roughly 30%.

items.t: Tupi/Iracema Field Returns to Reaching Production of 1 Million Barrels per Day

With this milestone, Petrobras resumes the production level achieved at the field in 2019 and confirms the pre-salt as one of the most competitive oil frontiers in the industry

The Tupi/Iracema field, located in the pre-salt of the Santos Basin, reached production of 1 million barrels per day this Friday (January 9), repeating the historic mark first achieved in 2019. The result is aligned with Petrobras' new 2026–2030 Business Plan, which foresees an increase in the oil and gas production curve through reservoir management and maximization of potential, improved production efficiency, increased water injection efficiency, and the mapping of new opportunities.

"We have always believed that Tupi/Iracema could return to producing at past levels. This asset is our first giant pre-salt field, with highly productive reservoirs. Our teams worked hard to ensure the resumption of production to a level consistent with the magnitude of the field. We are very proud to now operate two giants with potential above 1 million barrels per day: Tupi/Iracema and Búzios, both in the pre-salt of the Santos Basin," celebrates Magda Chambriard, president of Petrobras.

Throughout 2025, Petrobras connected eleven wells in Tupi/Iracema, which now has more than 150 drilled wells. The company is studying the construction of additional wells, as well as assessing the possibility of a new platform from 2031 onward and extending the service life of some of the nine existing units, guided by the objective of continuous value generation from the asset. The implementation of these activities is subject to the necessary approvals by the consortium and by the ANP, including the analysis of the request for license extension.

"This return of Tupi/Iracema to production of 1 million barrels per day reinforces that the pre-salt, over the past 16 years, has become one of the most competitive oil frontiers in the global industry and a cradle of innovations. A unique combination of giant reserves, high productivity, oil with a lower carbon footprint, and above-average efficiency," celebrates Petrobras' Executive Director of Exploration and Production, Sylvia Anjos.

Petrobras and Shell Raise Stakes in Brazil’s Atapu and Mero Pre-Salt Fields
sum: Petrobras and Shell have increased their participation in Brazil’s Atapu and Mero pre-salt reservoirs after securing additional equity in an auction held by Pré-Sal Petróleo (PPSA).

The consortium formed by Petrobras (80%), in partnership with Shell Brasil Petróleo (20%), acquired 3.500% participation in the production sharing agreement of the Mero shared reservoir, offering a final amount of $1.47 billion.
With this acquisition, Petrobras has increased its participation in the Mero shared reservoir from 38.60% to 41.40%.

Additionally, also in partnership with Shell (26.76%), Petrobras (73.24%) acquired 0.950% participation in the production sharing agreement of the Atapu shared reservoir, offering a final amount of $189 million. With this acquisition, Petrobras has boosted its share in the Atapu shared reservoir from 65.687% to 66.38%.
Shell Brasil increased its participating interest in the units from 16.663% to 16.917% in Atapu and from 19.3% to 20% in Mero.

Petrobras’ participation in the PPSA Non-Contracted Areas Auction is aligned with the company’s long-term strategy, reaffirmed in the Business Plan 2026-30, which foresees the replacement of its oil and gas reserves with economic and environmental resilience.

“Today’s winning bid reinforces our disciplined approach to grow Shell’s high margin portfolio in Brazil. Our assets in Brazil are among the most competitive in our global portfolio, combining strong performance with a low carbon footprint,” said Peter Costello, Shell’s Upstream President.

Novonor to retain 4% stake in Braskem
sum: Former Odebrecht will continue receiving dividends from petrochemical company with no decision-making power

Novonor will keep only 4% of Braskem’s preferred shares (nonvoting) as part of the process to transfer its stake—which currently gives it control of the petrochemical company, with 38.3% of total capital and 50.1% of voting shares—to a fund managed by IG4, according to people familiar with the matter. These shares are currently pledged as collateral to creditor banks of the former Odebrecht, which will participate in the deal without enforcing debts that now total R$19 billion.

As a minority shareholder in Braskem, Novonor will continue to receive dividends but will no longer take part in managing the business. Once the shares are transferred, the fund managed by IG4 and Petrobras will become the company’s main shareholders and will sign a new shareholders’ agreement, acting jointly in governance. Petrobras is currently Braskem’s second-largest shareholder, with 36.1% of total capital and 47% of voting shares.

Changes are expected in Braskem’s top leadership, following a broad restructuring one year ago, when only four executives were retained. According to the sources, IG4 will have the right to nominate the company’s next chief executive. Petrobras will take at least one of the vice-presidencies and secure a seat on the board of directors, alongside the asset manager.

Economist Helcio Tokeshi, managing partner at IG4, is considered the leading candidate for the CEO role, according to information published by Brazil Stock Guide and confirmed by Valor. Tokeshi also manages CLI, a port operator in IG4’s portfolio that the asset manager put up for sale this year. Petrobras’s nominee would be engineer Luiz Valente, currently a Braskem board member appointed by the state-owned oil giant and with extensive experience in the oil and gas industry.

A person close to IG4, however, said no final decision has been made regarding the composition of the new executive team, which will be chosen jointly with Petrobras. This source noted that the agreement provides for 90 days between signing and closing, as well as subsequent approval by Brazil’s antitrust regulator, CADE.

Investments are expected to move more than R$ 450 million for the recovery of the Amazon rainforest
ProFloresta+ encourages forest restoration in the Amazon, financed through the sale of carbon credits

Petrobras and the Brazilian Development Bank (BNDES) launched on Monday, the 10th, the first ProFloresta+ call for proposals to purchase 5 million high-integrity carbon credits. Five contracts will be signed for 1 million credits each, to be generated from the ecological restoration of at least 3,000 hectares per project, in private or public areas under forest concession within the Amazon biome, over a 25-year period.

"Our team is very optimistic about this first Petrobras transaction involving ecological restoration carbon credits. The expectation is that it will serve as a price and technical benchmark for generating high-quality carbon credits from the forest restoration of our biomes," said Petrobras' Director of Sustainability and Energy Transition, Angélica Laureano.

Petrobras structured the ProFloresta+ program in partnership with BNDES, aiming to provide financing to the developers of the projects selected through the call for proposals via special credit lines, such as the Climate Fund, with favorable rates and terms for ecological restoration projects that may last up to 25 years and have a financial cost of 1% per year. The call for proposals has the potential to generate more than R$ 450 million in investments.

"BNDES is helping to turn the forestry sector into a driver of the green economy. Through credit, non-reimbursable funds, and financial innovation, we are creating real conditions to scale up restoration and the sustainable use of our biomes. ProFloresta+ is an example of this vision: an instrument that will strengthen the high-integrity carbon market and generate tangible benefits for people and the planet," said Tereza Campello, BNDES's Director of Social and Environmental Affairs.
